# Database Schema Instructions

## Purpose
Define persistent table structure & relations (Drizzle) while remaining independent of domain logic.

## Artifacts
- `<root>.database-schema.ts`

## Naming
- Table constant: `<ENTITY>` (UPPER_SNAKE)
- Relations constant: `<ENTITY>Relations`

## Required Columns
- Always include: `id`, `uuid`, `status` (soft delete flag), audit timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt)
- Reuse shared fragments: `AUDIT_COLUMNS()` or equivalent helpers

## Column Rules
| Aspect | Rule |
|--------|------|
| Nullability | Prefer NOT NULL for required domain invariants |
| Enum | Use TypeScript enum mapped to `varchar` + constraint / check if needed |
| Foreign Keys | Use `references(() => OTHER.id)` explicit with `onDelete: 'cascade'` only when safe |
| Defaults | Database-generated; avoid duplicating defaults in domain unless invariant |

## Indexes & Constraints
- Add composite indexes for frequent filtered queries
- Unique index for `uuid`
- Document rationale in trailing comment above definition

## Relations Definition
```ts
export const <ENTITY>Relations = relations(<ENTITY>, ({ one, many }) => ({
  related: one(RELATED_ENTITY, { fields: [<ENTITY>.relatedId], references: [RELATED_ENTITY.id] }),
  relatedList: many(RELATED_ENTITY),
}));
```

## Anti-Patterns
- Do NOT embed JSON blobs for structured relational data without justification
- Avoid naming drift (table vs entity vs port)

## Quality Gates
- No `any` types
- Keep file limited to schema + relations only
- Run Codacy after edit
